item.title: Martin Wolf on the US midterms: What will the Democrats do next?
item.itunes:title: Martin Wolf on the US midterms: What will the Democrats do next?
item.itunes:subtitle: Paul Krugman explains what the party may do with their newfound power
item.description:
Americans roundly rejected the Republican Party under President Donald Trump at the ballot box, giving the Democratic Party control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. That means Democrats have a raft of new tools with which to oppose Trump, including control of investigative committees the party may use to look into alleged corruption. How should the Democrats use that power? Does the scale of their victory mean they have the country’s backing, or just that Republicans were unpopular? And will Trump’s brand of politics return? Martin speaks to Nobel prize-winning economist Paul Krugman to discuss what happens next.


To enjoy future episodes, be sure to subscribe to ‘Martin Wolf on the World’ wherever you get your podcasts. You can also watch Martin’s podcast series on the FT’s YouTube channel here: https://www.youtube.com/@FinancialTimes

item.title: Why investors soured on the Democrats
item.itunes:title: Why investors soured on the Democrats
item.itunes:subtitle: Nasdaq plunges in chaotic trading as Democratic ‘blue wave’ upends AI bets
item.description:
US tech stocks plunged over worries that the blue wave could slow down the AI boom, and the FT’s Joe Miller explains what stance a Democratic Congress may take towards AI. Plus, the UK government is preparing to extend Palantir’s controversial £330mn health contract, Paraguay’s president Santiago Peña has resigned after the collapse of a big digital bank, and the Bank of England raised interest rates to try to tackle surging inflation.


Mentioned in this podcast:

Nasdaq plunges in chaotic trading as Democratic ‘blue wave’ upends AI bets

Trump’s tech cheerleaders brace for bipartisan backlash

‘The money didn’t work’: Big Tech’s $600mn midterm campaign falls flat

Paraguay’s pro-Trump president resigns over bank collapse

Bank of England raises interest rates to 4% in bid to tame inflation

UK planning to not trigger Palantir break clause but make it fight for NHS contract

item.title: How will the Democrats’ sweep shape policy and markets?
item.itunes:title: How will the Democrats’ sweep shape policy and markets?
item.itunes:subtitle: Their win may usher in more regulation, but investors seem unfazed
item.description:
Washington will have trouble getting things done with a gridlocked government after this week’s midterm elections, but it’s hard to tell whether US President Donald Trump will use the defeat as a chance to soften his foreign policy stance. Plus, investors are feeling optimistic about a return to normalcy following Democrats’ massive victory, and Russia agreed to supply Iran with 90 launchers for advanced guided missiles.


Mentioned in this podcast:

Stocks surge after Democrats’ midterms sweep

item.itunes:subtitle: Democrats poised to win control of Congress
item.description:
The Democrats score massive wins in the US midterm elections, bond investors are feeling optimistic about the make-up of the next Congress, and Qatar’s state-owned energy company is on track to become the world’s biggest buyer of US liquefied natural gas by early next decade. Plus, a massive fraud scandal in Turkey is starting to weigh on the country’s economy.

item.title: The Gulf braces for new strikes against Iran
item.itunes:title: The Gulf braces for new strikes against Iran
item.itunes:subtitle: Diplomats warn that renewed conflict would be even more damaging than previous rounds of fighting
item.description:
A Democratic-controlled Congress may struggle to ease cost of living pressures and Middle East diplomats warn that renewed conflict between the US and Iran would be even more damaging than previous rounds of fighting. Serbia shuts down a bank favoured by Russians as it enters a new political era. Plus, Binance has started letting customers withdraw funds after the world's biggest crypto exchange experienced a record $6.3bn hack.

Gulf braced for escalation of war between US-Israel alliance and Iran
